items.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Games That Are Barely Playable Today
items.summary: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

items.title: Skate is dropping seasons and season passes in favor of 'regular, agile content updates'
items.summary:
A little over a year after EA launched Skate into early access—where it remains—developer Full Circle is removing the seasonal structure that has underpinned the game so far, saying that doing so will give the team "the freedom to launch features earlier in their lifecycle."

Skate got off to a bit of a rough start when it went live in September 2025, and while it's turned around the initially iffy response from players, it hasn't gone entirely smoothly since then. An initial promise that no new maps would be locked behind paywalls was chucked out the window in February, and Full Circle laid off employees that same month, saying that cutting headcounts means it can "better support Skate's long-term future and focus the team on the things that matter most to you."

The end of Skate's seasonal structure is less overtly not good than those moves, but it is a sign that things aren't going quite as Full Circle had envisioned, and the message that it's still "committed to keep driving Skate forward" has a certain 'despite everything' tone that doesn't strike me as the sort of thing you say when when all cylinders are firing.

"The game is still a work in progress, and we're using this valuable time to experiment, iterate, and figure out what works best for the long-term health of the game—especially when it comes to social features and progression," the studio wrote. "Ultimately, we want to build Skate in a way that lets us roll out fresh content much faster, even if it's not totally finished yet."

items.title: Microsoft announces it's deprecating the Telnet client in Windows, giving me a sudden flashback to when I used to use Telnet
items.summary:
In its latest update on deprecated features in Windows , Microsoft casually mentioned that "Telnet Client is deprecated and will be removed from Windows in a future release."

This may not mean much to you if you didn't do a lot of computer networking in the 1990s or earlier, but the text-based protocol for remotely opening command-line interfaces was a workhorse we used for a bunch of things. It's how antique university lab computers that didn't even have Netscape Navigator installed connected to the internet, how I played text-based online games like the Discworld MUD back in the day, and how we used to connect to our routers.

By default, Telnet didn't encrypt all the data it was swapping back and forth between computers, which is why it's since been replaced by tools like SSH and PowerShell. So it's not a surprise that it's being deprecated, and honestly I'm impressed that it outlived both WordPad and Cortana . 

A Windows feature being deprecated means that it won't be in active development and is a candidate for removal in a future update, so Telnet isn't being 86ed immediately. If you're still using it to test network connections because that's what you're used to then carry on as you were, but get ready to grumble and switch over to PowerShell when Microsoft finally does pull the plug.
items.t: Microsoft announces it's deprecating the Telnet client in Windows, giving me a sudden flashback to when I used to use Telnet

The announcement streams aren't just marketing, he explained, they help dictate what kinds of things the team should focus on with every update. If it doesn't sound exciting enough to rally players around a new league, it doesn't get made.

After a teaser trailer reveals the theme and title of the league a few weeks before the full announcement, the stream dives right into the juiciest details—an approach that Rogers believes is paramount when it comes to selling the update.

Just prior to that, Team Cherry surprised everyone by announcing that the Hollow Knight: Silksong launch was imminent, and Aeternum—and a whole bunch of others —decided the smart move was to just get out of the way.

Well, here we go again. Yesterday, Team Cherry announced that " Cherry Time " is coming on November 27, with "a bunch of exciting announcements, plus an update on Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow," the Silksong expansion announced in December 2025. Some fans are hoping that means the Sea of Sorrow release date will be announced—or maybe even that it will actually be released.

Whatever's coming, Aeternum says that this time around, it's standing firm.

"Dear Team Cherry," Aeternum wrote in an Official Statement: Part 2 message, riffing on the "Official Statement" it put out in 2025. "A little over a year ago, just as we were about to launch our game, you announced Silksong. "Now here we are again, just days from launch. Aeterna Lucis, our new Metroidvania, comes out on December 3... and you announce Cherry Time.

"This time we're staying put. Not to…

items.title: "This isn't a sign to retreat": Rockstar's historic union vote has failed, with 75% voting against, but the organisers are going to "keep fighting"
items.summary:
The potentially historic vote at GTA 6 creators Rockstar Games on whether to seek formal union recognition has failed, the International Workers of Great Britain have announced. Around 1600 studio members cast ballots across 12th to 26th November , even as the company's open world Bonnie & Clyde 'em up released onto PlayStation and Xbox storefronts. In the end, approximately 25% of the participants voted in favour.

According to the IWGB themselves, "the result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organising with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives."

Speaking to RPS in an emailed statement, Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe argued that the vote's failure "reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong." The IWGB, meanwhile, have declared that "this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for". They're going to keep mobilising for more labour power, with the failed vote now framed as a foot in the door.
items.t: "This isn't a sign to retreat": Rockstar's historic union vote has failed, with 75% voting against, but the organisers are going to "keep fighting"

With thousands of enterable buildings , unpredictable and slightly scary NPCs , and systems that help you determine what kind of criminal you want to be. It all really does feel like a milestone for what videogames can do.

"As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, says in an interview with Eurogamer. "So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun." 

(Image credit: Rockstar Games) The sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile , a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating. There's Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable. The more stealthy and non-lethal you are, the higher your profile will be. It's similar to Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor System .

items.title: Rockstar workers vote overwhelmingly against union recognition
items.summary:
After two weeks of voting that bracketed the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, Rockstar Games employees have voted overwhelmingly against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. 

25% of Rockstar employees voted in favor of the recognition agreement, the union said, while 75% voted against it. 1,544 employees took part in the vote, representing a turnout of just over 93%.

Rockstar workers actually founded a union earlier this year—the Rockstar Game Workers Union, a subsidiary of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain—and it will continue to operate as it has. The IWGB said the outcome will not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing or exercising union rights, but the company will not be required to regularly meet with union representatives for collective bargaining or other relevant matters. 

Despite the vote, the union said it will continue with organizing efforts at Rockstar.

"For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues," the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union said. "We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

"Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions…
items.t: Rockstar workers vote overwhelmingly against union recognition

items.title: How to steal the Bravado Banshee in GTA 6
items.summary:
The Bravado Banshee is another one of the cars you'll need to track down for Randy in GTA 6 , but unlike the Pegassi Infernus , this one doesn't involve anything as dodgy as robbing a police lockup. 

You can find this car inside the Sunrise Premium Autos showroom at the north tip of Southside, southwest of Pay 'N' Spray - Salton or east across the road from Ron Gas - Southside. This region is to the northeast of Hamlet. 

There are two showrooms here, so make sure you have the right one, though the other does contain Pfister Growlers, in case you haven't gotten that car for Randy yet, either. Head inside to find the car—if you've played previous GTAs, you'll recognise it as a convertible with a white stripe down the middle. Hop inside, use the key cloner, and drive it through the glass. 

This might damage it a bit, but you can always repair it at Ron Gas nearby, or at the gas station near Randy's shop. Just remember to drive fast, and if the tracker starts to beep, speed up to stop it pinging your location to the cops. Delivering this one gets you 6,500k and a 5k condition bonus as usual if it's in good nick.
